title: Enterprise security Q&A and contract language draft - SOC2/ISO/HIPAA
content:
Purpose:
This is a working go-to-market brief for sales and AE teams to use when discussing Redwood’s security posture with enterprise prospects. Focus: SOC2, ISO27001 alignment, HIPAA readiness (for PHI processing scenarios), and practical audit / log language that can be shared in early contract negotiations.

Audience:
- AEs and solutions engineers preparing for enterprise conversations
- Sales leadership building rebuttals/objections
- Legal & security reviewers who will finalize contractual language

Status & intent:
- Draft: tactical language and Q&A for deals in pipeline.
- Legal must sign off before inclusion in SOWs/contract exhibits.
- Uses: discovery call one-pagers, RFP responses, early-stage contract redlines.

One-line positioning statements (for pitch):
- "Redwood Inference: production-grade inference with enterprise-grade controls — SOC2-aligned operations, ISO-ready policies, and a HIPAA-capable private deployment model for regulated data."
- "We keep customer data in customer-controlled networks for private deployments and provide detailed, tamper-evident telemetry for compliance auditing."

Key proof points (short):
- SOC2 Type II: operational control matrix in place; rolling assessments (Q4 2024 report available to prospects under NDA).
- ISO27001: core policies and gap remediation plan completed; certification in targeted regions by mid-2025.
- HIPAA readiness: private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) plus KMS integrations and BAAs available for qualifying contracts.
- Audit trails: per-request metadata retention, signed append-only logs (immutable storage options), and exportable CSV/JSON for auditors.

Suggested contract / SOW language (sales-friendly drafts — send to Legal):
1) Data handling scope: 
   - "Customer Data" means data uploaded, provided, or generated by the Customer via Redwood services. Redwood will process Customer Data only to provide the Services and as instructed by Customer.

2) Data residency / segregation: 
   - "Customer may specify region(s) for hosting. For Private deployments, Redwood will deploy within Customer's VPC or on-prem environment per the deployment schedule in Exhibit A. For Hosted deployments, Redwood will use the region(s) elected by Customer and documented in the order form."

3) Encryption / key management: 
   - "All in-transit data is encrypted using TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption is provided using AES-256. For customers requiring key ownership, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or HSM-based key storage for Private deployments."

4) Audit logs & evidence: (core ask from compliance teams)
   - "Redwood will retain system and request-level audit logs for a period of ninety (90) days by default. Upon Customer request, Redwood will retain the audit trail for up to [custom period] for an additional fee. Audit logs include timestamp, requesting API key ID, model/version used, token counts, request/response digests (not full PII/PHI payload by default), and routing/compute metadata. Logs are exportable in JSON/CSV format and can be delivered via secure link or SFTP under a documented process."
   - Note for Legal: include an exhibit describing the exact log schema and allowed fields to avoid over-sharing PHI.

5) Breach notification / incident response: 
   - "Redwood will notify Customer of confirmed incidents affecting Customer Data within 72 hours of detection, provide initial impact assessment, and cooperate in forensic review. Root cause analysis and remediation timeline will be provided as deliverables."

6) HIPAA & BAA clause (template language):
   - "Where Customer indicates PHI will be provided, Redwood will execute a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and comply with the applicable provisions of HIPAA. For hosted deployments, Redwood will implement technical and administrative safeguards consistent with HIPAA Security Rule. For highest-assurance use cases, Customer is advised to use Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) with customer-controlled keys.)"

7) SLA & fallback controls for compliance availability: 
   - "Redwood offers Dedicated capacity with committed throughput and targeted 99.9% uptime for inference endpoints. For critical workloads, customers can configure cross-region failover and model fallback policies to maintain continuity."

Sales Q&A (concise answers for rapid reuse):
Q: "Do you have SOC2?"
A: "We maintain SOC2-aligned controls and run annual Type II audits — summary report available under NDA. Contact security@redwoodinference.com to start the process."

Q: "Can we get access to raw request logs for auditing?"
A: "Yes: we provide request-level audit exports with metadata and digests. For PHI workflows, we redact or restrict sensitive payloads and work with your security team to define an approved schema and delivery mechanism."

Q: "How do you prevent data leakage across customers?"
A: "Isolation is multi-layered: tenant isolation at runtime, per-customer model pinning, KV/prefix cache partitioning, and dedicated pools for high-compliance customers. Private and Dedicated modes offer stronger isolation guarantees than shared-hosted tiers."

Q: "Is Redwood ISO27001 certified?"
A: "We are actively aligning controls and expect certification in targeted regions in 2025; meanwhile, we can provide policy artifacts and gap remediation evidence."

Q: "What's your encryption posture?"
A: "TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest, and support for customer-managed keys via standard KMS/HSM integrations."

Competitive notes (what to call out vs competitors):
- Primary angle: "serving-first" security — not just model access. Emphasize runtime isolation (dedicated pools), observability (token-level cost + traceability), and easy exportable evidence for audits.
- Competitor A: strong on data access APIs but limited model-level isolation; call out Redwood’s per-model pinning and cache partitioning as differentiators.
- Competitor B: offers managed endpoints but lacks turnkey BAAs for hosted; Redwood’s Private/VPC + BAA path is a counter.
- Competitor C: fully self-hosted runtimes requiring customer ops investment — position Redwood as less ops-heavy with enterprise controls baked in.

Trade-offs & risk notes for deals:
- Hosted convenience vs. compliance risk: advise customers handling PHI to choose Private or Dedicated.
- Log retention vs. privacy: some customers demand full payload logging — we should push to provide digests & metadata instead and only log payloads under strict contract terms.
- Legal review cycles: audit schema exhibit must be finalized early in large deals to avoid last-minute redlines; add to discovery checklist.

Open items / questions for Security & Legal (owners):
- Define canonical audit log schema (owner: SRE/Product; due: 2025-03-15) — includes which fields contain redaction rules.
- Finalize BAA template and exhibit with HIPAA-specific technical safeguards (owner: Legal - Samir; due: 2025-03-22).
- Clarify default log retention and paid extension pricing (owner: Revenue Ops; due: 2025-03-10).

Suggested next steps (actionable):
1) Review draft with Legal and Security — schedule 60-min sync (owner: Priya).
2) Produce a 1-page "security one-pager" for AEs summarizing the above (owner: Marketing).
3) Add audit schema as an Exhibit to the standard Order Form (owner: Contracts).
4) Create a small engineering spike to produce a sample export (JSON/CSV) and automated delivery flow for audit requests (owner: SRE).

Notes to AE & Solutions teams (informal):
- Use the Q&A language verbatim in discovery emails; flag any customer requests for full payload logs ASAP.
- Avoid promising certification dates — use "targeted" or "in progress" language until Legal confirms.

Appendix: quick log-field examples (for internal review only)
- timestamp: 2025-02-10T14:12:03Z
- request_id: rqd_01EXAMPLE
- api_key_id: cust_1234
- model: redwood-model-v2
- model_commit: sha256:abcd...
- route: hosted/us-west-2
- token_count_input: 42
- token_count_output: 128
- response_digest: sha256:efgh... (useful for integrity check without storing payload)
- user_agent: Redwood-SDK/1.3.0

-- end of draft --

Internal comments (loose / notes to self):
- Consider a field-level redaction toolkit for customers who need selective PHI persistency.
- Explore pricing for extended log retention and forensic exports (monthly vs one-time).
- Capture customer audit needs in Salesforce opportunity record (checkboxes: BAA required, log retention >365d, ISO evidence required).

Prepared by: Priya Raman (GTMSec lead)
Last updated: 2025-03-01
